Definition: from G4536; to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively):--(which are yet to) sound (a trumpet).
BiblicalUsage: The Greek word salpízō means to trumpet, that is sound a blast (literally or figuratively). In 1 Corinthians 15:52, we read, "…twinkling of an eye, at the last trump…"; in Matthew 6:2, "Therefore when thou doest alms, do not sound…". You hear it again in Revelation 8:6 — "…seven angels which had the seven trumpets prepared…" — and in Revelation 8:7, "The first angel sounded, and there followed hail…".
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that salpízō is no accident in the text, and it names something real, and God does not use empty words. And I hold that salpízō is as true now as when it was first written, because God does not change.
